subsystems.name: Electrodes
subsystems.role: pick up microvolt-level electrical activity from the scalp through hair and skin.

subsystems.name: Analog front end
subsystems.role: amplify and digitize tiny brain signals while rejecting noise and motion artifacts.

subsystems.name: Processing unit
subsystems.role: run real-time signal processing and classification algorithms on the headband.

subsystems.name: Power and connectivity
subsystems.role: supply power and stream data wirelessly to a phone or computer.

subsystems.name: Mechanical housing
subsystems.role: hold sensors against the head comfortably, especially during sleep.

subsystems.name: Software and algorithms
subsystems.role: translate brain waves into sleep stages, focus scores and wellness feedback.

buildSteps.title: Design sensor layout and ergonomics
buildSteps.detail: Decide how many electrodes, where they sit on the scalp, and how the band will stay comfortable through a night's sleep.

buildSteps.title: Fabricate electrodes and frame
buildSteps.detail: Mould conductive elastomer or metal pins into a flexible headband, ensuring good contact without conductive gel.

buildSteps.title: Assemble electronics
buildSteps.detail: Solder the analog front end, microcontroller, radio and power management onto a small circuit board.

buildSteps.title: Write firmware
buildSteps.detail: Program the board to sample EEG, filter line noise and movement artifacts, and stream data over Bluetooth.

buildSteps.title: Develop algorithms
buildSteps.detail: Train machine-learning models on labelled sleep and focus data to classify stages and attention levels.

buildSteps.title: Build the app and cloud pipeline
buildSteps.detail: Create a mobile app that syncs data, shows trends and delivers insights or closed-loop audio cues.

buildSteps.title: Validate against clinical standards
buildSteps.detail: Compare sleep staging with polysomnography in sleep labs to measure accuracy and reliability.

buildSteps.title: Manufacture and test
buildSteps.detail: Scale production, run quality control on every unit, and ship with instructions for safe, comfortable use.

prerequisites.why: they let a headband work without gel, which is essential for home sleep and wellness use.
EEG signals are only a few microvolts, so amplification must be extremely quiet.
it provides a low-power wireless link to phones and tablets.
automated staging is improving but still less accurate than clinical polysomnography.
models need large, diverse labelled datasets to generalise across people and nights.

pathway.milestone: single-channel dry EEG headbands for sleep tracking and meditation
pathway.unlocks: affordable, home-based awareness of sleep and focus patterns.

pathway.milestone: multi-channel headbands with improved comfort and accuracy, validated in sleep labs
pathway.unlocks: more reliable staging and broader clinical research use.

pathway.milestone: closed-loop auditory or electrical stimulation to enhance slow-wave sleep
pathway.unlocks: active sleep improvement rather than passive tracking.

pathway.milestone: integration with medical-grade diagnostics and other biometrics
pathway.unlocks: home screening for sleep disorders and personalised wellness programmes.
